The Portable Wireless Network Monitor puts your grid in your pocket.

The first right-click binds it to you; further right-clicks cycle the HUD Off, Normal and Scientific. Sneak-right-click §drebinds it to the player holding it§r.

It also works from any §dBaubles§r accessory slot, and shows live EU, EU/t rate and a GT-style power tier on servers as well as in single player.

§6Portable charging:§r shapelessly craft this terminal with one rechargeable battery to install it. It remains the same item, without separate variants. Battery capacity and voltage tier determine the buffer and charging rate; the new battery's existing charge enters the buffer immediately. While carried in inventory or a Baubles slot, a partly empty buffer requests a full refill from the bound wireless grid every §110 seconds (200 ticks)§r. The grid also pays the downlink loss: supplied EU × (1 + downlink loss fraction).

Compatible electric tools in inventory, armor and Baubles slots are charged simultaneously, at §11A × battery voltage per tool§r, limited by the remaining buffer. Charging preserves held-tool use and mining, avoiding interruptions caused by charge updates.

To replace the battery, shapelessly craft the equipped terminal with a new battery. The new battery retains its own charge. The old battery inherits the remaining terminal buffer and returns to inventory, or drops on the ground if inventory is full. A chat tip appears on first acquisition, then after §110§r and §120 minutes§r of continued possession, for §13 tips§r in total.

A terminal with a battery adds a charging status above the three existing HUD lines: Buffer empty, Standby, Charging, and Fully charged. After charging ends with no new demand for §11 second§r, Fully charged appears for §15 seconds§r before Standby; new demand resumes Charging immediately.

Toggle the charging line with §3/gtswn hud charge on/off§r. Toggle energy, instantaneous rate and average rate with §3/gtswn hud eu on/off§r, §3/gtswn hud instant on/off§r and §3/gtswn hud average on/off§r. All four lines have configuration options; commands save the corresponding settings.
